title.narrative: WGG- Research and Documentation in Uganda

description.narrative: The strategy of research and documentation is integral to the learning and evidence building agenda of the WGG Consortium and its country-level strategic partners. There are significant programmatic components of the consortium wide joint activities as part of global and regional advocacy efforts.

sector.narrative: Support for feminist, women-led and women's rights organisations and movements, and institutions (governmental and non-govermental) at all levels to enhance their effectiveness, influence and substainability (activities and core-funding). These organisations exist to bring about transformative change for gender equality and/or the rights of women and girls in developing countries. Their activities include agenda-setting, advocacy, policy dialogue, capacity development, awareness raising and prevention, service provision, conflict-prevention and peacebuilding, research, organising, and alliance and network building

Building on the CREA-Femme Forte and akili Dada led SELF Academy, Femme Forte led a SELF Action project in Uganda in 2024. Using the Authentic Voices manual developed by Femme Forte, and with the support of the appointed focal point leads/ teachers, three clubs across three schools were formed: The Expression Health Club at Manjasi High School (Eastern Region), The SELF Health Club at Erussi Secondary School (West Nile), and the Mental Health Club at Kansanga Secondary School (Central Region). Each of the three clubs comprised 30 young girls and supported the students to democratically elect their club leaders.
Two Training of trainers workshops with 20 participants in each

In August 2022, CREA's partner, hosted a capacity building session to educate participants, including girls and women with disabilities and their aides, on leadership roles and responsibilities. The session focused on ending GBV and SGBV in their communities, increasing their power and influence, and promoting self-care, collective wellness, and healing for women leaders and rights activists.A 2-day session on SGBV took place in November 2022, in Kampala. This session highlighted reporting mechanisms, services, and the importance of safeguarding, and roles and responsibilities of leaders of girls and women with disabilities in ending SGBV. As a result of these sessions, 46 leaders have reported cases of violence to the authorities, mobilized and sensitized fellow girls and women with disabilities, and have received special invitations from their districts.CREA hosted one SELF academy: a young girls leadership academy; out of 28 participants, 2 were young girls with disability. They were capacity strengthened on feminist leadership, using art for activism and sexual and reproductive health and rights.

In partnership with the Makerere 89th guild, Femme Forte conducted the Meet Your Leader round table Equip Circle under the “Top of Form series,” these are capacity-building sessions aimed at nurturing and mentoring young women leaders. The activity aimed at mentorship in leadership for young women leaders. Through two equip circles on feminist leadership, FF trained 71 Young Women on feminist transformative leadership to increase their capacities to conduct human rights advocacy toward developing inclusive and progressive norms on SGBV and political participation, while enriching them with knowledge on feminist grounding.
